decision: Store lineage (actor, via, at, reason, change) inside each event's payload as a `meta` argument on the Imported, ValueSet and ValueRemoved events, so it survives restarts
reason: Lineage is stored in the events themselves, so it survives restarts

decision: Represent actor as {kind, id}; imports and file edits are recorded with actor {kind: unknown, id: null}
When TROUPE_ACTOR is unset, default the actor to a human with the login name from getpass.getuser(); if that lookup fails, the id is None
Validate TROUPE_ACTOR by splitting on the first ':'; it needs a separator, a kind of human or agent, and a non-empty id, otherwise it raises UsageError (exit 2)
Format `at` as a UTC timestamp with microseconds and a 'Z' suffix
Add a `--reason TEXT` option to `set` only; reason is null otherwise
Use a fresh uuid4 change id per command, shared by all of that command's events; a set that first reconciles hand edits produces two separate changes
Compute the CLI lineage (and timestamp) at record time inside the lock, after reconcile, rather than up front, while still validating the actor up front
Move the lineage helpers out of store.py into a new module src/troupe/lineage.py
reason: so the CLI doesn't pull eventsourcing in at import time

decision: Drop the automated legacy-database test and verify compatibility by hand against the previous commit's code
reason: The test couldn't fake old event topics in-process; building an old-format database needs the previous commit's code

decision: Fill in `at` for legacy events from the event store's stored timestamp instead of leaving it null
reason: `at: null` breaks the RFC 3339 timestamp contract

decision: Set `via` to null for legacy set/remove events (changed from an initial 'file')
reason: It was never recorded whether they came from the CLI or a file, and the allowed values have no 'unknown'

decision: Give all legacy imports one shared change id 'unrecorded-import' and each legacy set/remove its own 'unrecorded-<seq>' id; these are not UUIDs
reason: Legacy imports all came from a single first-run command, so they should share one change id

decision: Match legacy changes to stored events by zipping config.changes with the stored events after the Created event
Initially validate TROUPE_ACTOR only in `set`, and escalate to the owner whether all commands should reject a malformed value
reason: Other commands record no CLI changes; the spec could be read either way

decision: Every config command (get, show, set, history, watch) rejects a malformed TROUPE_ACTOR with exit 2, empty stdout and a stderr message
reason: The Lineage section's rule covers any CLI command (owner answer)

decision: Parse the actor as the very first step of run(), before the theatre is resolved and before any reconcile, import or write
reason: so nothing is touched on a bad value

decision: Test bad actors with five malformed values across all five commands, checking for no events.sqlite created and an unchanged config file
test_lineage checks the timestamp format with a regex that allows optional fractional seconds, and checks that timestamps are in sorted order
Document lineage, including legacy behaviour, in the README
